newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos orders army to hunt down kidnap gangs.
newsitem.headline: Ramos orders army to hunt down kidnap gangs.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos ordered the army on Wednesday to take over the campaign against kidnap gangs in the troubled southern Philippines after a senior aide admitted the situation had worsened.

Interior Secretary Robert Barbers recommended the use of the army, saying bigger and better-equipped forces were needed to fight criminals and rebels who have kidnapped 38 people, mostly businessmen, in the region since January, the presidential palace said.

"Kidnapping has taken a turn for the worst. Insurgents and other lawless groups have resorted to kidnapping to advance their cause and to destabilise local society," Barbers said in a report to Ramos released to media.
The army will replace the police in the anti-kidnapping campaign, a palace statement said.
About 2,000 residents of Cotabato city in Maguindanao province, where most of the kidnappings have occurred, held a protest march last week to demand strong action against kidnap-for-ransom gangs.
The protest coincided with a funeral procession for a Filipino-Chinese businessman killed by his abductors even though his family had paid ransom.
Cotabato businessmen recently threatened to shut down their establishments in protest against the government filure to stop kidnap gangs.

Kidnapping has become a booming business in the Philippines, with the amount of ransom paid to gangs in the first three months of this year already exceeding the 142 million pesos ($5.4 million) they collected for all of 1996, anti-crime groups said.
Families of victims generally refuse to report to the police because of widespread suspicion, officialy acknowledged in some cases, that policemen themselves are protecting the kidnappers.
